Legends Artwork page: native source reconstruction
================================================

Source images are the reference and classic files in
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. Their identities are respectively
PE:6a70a6d9:02711000 and PE:6a70b91c:0270a000. All addresses below are Reference
RVAs; native-sources.tsv retains the actual independently read Classic operands.
tools/extract_artwork_description_catalog.py reads both images afresh with the
configured native objdump. It does not execute a game function, translator,
translation-data generator or test. The assembly and TSV are source evidence,
not an observed display result or acceptance report.

The screenshot's page entry is 0xd4bf70..0xd4c427 (Classic
0xd48fb0..0xd49467). It explicitly creates/searches Legends tabs with
tab.type at +0x20 equal to 7 and tab.id at +0x24. It resolves a stored artwork
ID into an art_image_chunk and a 0..499 image index. The page obtains its title
from image.name at +0x38 with personal-name formatter 0xa94030. Empty titles
produce Untitled. A missing image produces This artwork has been lost. instead
of entering the paragraph formatter. These caller branches are absent from
the paragraph's own string list, and are retained in this extraction.

Paragraph call at 0xd4c350 (Classic 0xd49390):
  art_image::getDescription 0x1451b10..0x145312c
                         (Classic 0x144ca80..0x144e09c)
  r9 = false: do not suppress original design quality and artist
  argument 5 = true: include the physical source
  argument 6 = true: include full element/action descriptions and history
  placement = -1; rendition quality = -1; copy author = -1
  plain separator = false; native LPAGE markup = true

Consequently this page is identified by native tab.type 7, not an English first
sentence or a particular creature noun. A null source takes the normal placement
path, where -1 produces It is a/an ... . An unhandled source kind, or an invalid
coin reference, also reaches the It is a prefix. The page can contain independent
action sentences and native wrapped links as well as This artwork ... sentences.

Whole paragraph order
---------------------
  physical_source_sentence? + main_image_sentence + property_sentences*
    + history_sentence? + entity_relation_sentence?

source.kind is queried through image.ref virtual +0x10 at 0x1451c14:
  0: This artwork appears on ARTIFACT_OR_BOOK.
     Artifact/book link kind follows actual item type and item flags. A missing
     artifact record produces an unknown artifact. Its saved name comes from
     the artifact name structure through 0xa94030.
  5: This artwork appears on a ITEM [and was crafted in SITE].
     placement 4 instead uses This work of art is a ITEM. Placement here is -1.
     ITEM is shared item noun 0xa82c10 with source item kind, subtype, material.
     SITE is image.site at +0xc4, resolved by 0x7db20 and named by 0xa94030.
     An unresolved creation site suppresses the optional clause.
  6: This artwork appears [on the front of / on the back of] COIN_DESIGNATION.
     Front/back selection is image.spec_ref_type 17/18. Other values retain
     the prefix without a side. Source coin record index is bounds checked;
     invalid indexes suppress that source sentence. 0x5be970 supplies the
     currency designation before the shared coin item noun 0xa82c10.
  7: This engraving appears on a floor/wall [in SITE / somewhere].
     Floor is source WORD +8 == 0x2b; all other values select wall.
  8: This artwork is a/an ORIGINAL_IMAGE.
     This directly continues into the original design quality; it adds no
     separate It is a sentence.
  other: no recognized physical-source sentence; continue with It is a/an.

Physical source sentences use .[B] in this page's argument mode; the alternate
caller mode uses period followed by two spaces. After recognized kinds 0/5/6/7,
the original image begins with It is a. Both paths are preserved as native source.

The shared placement superset also has The item, On the item, On the front of
the coin, On the coin's back, and Engraved [on the floor/on the wall] prefixes,
each followed by is a. These are shared callers' branches; the Artwork page
sets placement=-1. Likewise the rendition branch requires physical_source=false
and source.kind==8, so it does not occur through this page's current call.
It remains extracted as shared grammar: separate rendition quality 1..5,
optional copy artist, rendition of, optional original image title and comma,
then the original design quality/image/material/original artist.

Original image
--------------
  article + design_quality? + image
    + (of ELEMENT_LIST)? + (in MATERIAL)? + (by ARTIST)? + .

Design quality 1..5: well-designed, finely-designed, superiorly designed,
exceptionally designed, masterfully designed. Zero/outside the finite range has
no quality adjective. Quality changes the native a/an fragment. Suppression of
quality/artist is a shared call argument, false here. image.elements being empty
suppresses the entire of clause; a material can still follow, so image in MATERIAL
is a complete native production. Materials are resolved from image +0xb4/+0xb8
by 0x14d1920; material RAW selection, state selection, and adjective selection
are retained as typed material suppliers. Artist ID +0xc0 is resolved as an
historical figure; live unit/identity naming takes priority when available,
otherwise its saved historical name supplies the by clause. Empty names suppress
that clause. Personal names, nicknames, generated names and title links retain
their native field and LPAGE boundaries; English letters do not imply a constant.

Element dispatch: six concrete/base classes
------------------------------------------
Main image calls element virtual +0x38 at 0x145274a. Action subject and object
use the same formatter with definite=true. The TSV retains both editions' real
vtable operands for base, creature, item, shape, plant and tree.
  base: empty string. Its actual leaf 0x72280..0x7229a clears either the heap or
    inline std::string buffer; both return branches are retained. The main image
    decides whether to add of solely from vector count, never from returned text.
    It unconditionally calls +0x38 and appends the result, then adds comma/and by
    element index. One stored empty element therefore produces image of .;
    two empty elements produce image of  and .; three produce image of ,  and .
    Material and artist clauses still follow independently. This is the actual
    virtual/pasting behavior, not a claim that the current displayed image or
    ordinary world generator has created a base element.
  creature: RAW race/caste; historical figure name and species; named/unnamed
    deity. Deity domains come from the full 130-way sphere table, with the native
    article selector for dawn/moon/night/rain/seasons/sky/stars/sun/weather/wind.
    Deity form composes skeletal, rotting, ghostly, needed female/male, and actual
    race/caste; domains are listed in the native reversed vector order.
  item: full type/subtype/material shared item noun; artifact lookup by real item
    ID; named artifact, unnamed artifact identity, titled book, and copy status.
  shape: descriptor_shape RAW NAME singular/plural and selected RAW ADJ.
  plant and tree: plant RAW NAME singular/plural; two virtual owners share one
    actual formatter.
Count 1 is singular; count >=2 uses native number words and plural; count 0 is an
unnumbered plural group. The complete native number-word function is preserved,
including 0..19 and tens 2..9 switch entries and scale/negative/remainder grammar.
The installed shape/adjective combinations and RAW provenance remain in
data/extracted/statue-art-sources.tsv, not invented as C++ string constants here.

Property dispatch and complete action switches
---------------------------------------------
Properties call virtual +0x28 at 0x14529da. Base property is empty. Transitive
0x146750 uses verb-1, 46 entries covering verbs 1..46. Intransitive 0x146eb0 has
48 entries covering 0..47. native-sources.tsv preserves all jump targets, including
the native empty/default entries. Every singular/plural action production is
retained in data/extracted/statue-art-sources.tsv and fully reconstructed in
data/runtime/statue-description-grammar.md section 4.
Valid empty/default actions emit SUBJECT. rather than an empty string. Invalid
subject indexes, and invalid transitive object indexes, instead return empty.
Count 1 selects is/looks/itself; count !=1 selects are/look/themselves. Definite
creature/shape/plant/item names, repeated group roles, named figures and deities
are supplied by the element graph, not split by guessed English list delimiters.

Historical subject and collection
---------------------------------
Full-description=false suppresses both history and organization suffixes; this
page passes true. A valid image.event produces The artwork relates to EVENT;
event virtual +0xd8 is called at 0x1452aaa. Reverse scan of all event collections
finds the latest containing collection and appends during COLLECTION, calling
virtual +0x30 at 0x1452b4d. Both scopes finish with period/two spaces.
The complete concrete event/collection graph is independently retained for both
editions in data/extracted/artwork-history-native: 133 event roots and 18
collection roots, their transitive direct callees, selectors, indirect typed
leaves, and full native function bodies. This extraction deliberately reuses
that full historical scope, rather than a selection of screenshot event phrases.

Organization suffix and dynamic profession supplier
---------------------------------------------------
Requires image.spec_ref_type==24, a valid entity reference and a valid index
into entity.art_image_types. Category 0 is The image is the symbol of; category 1
is The image was commissioned by. Other category values contribute no relation
predicate but continue with The image and the entity description. That native
default branch is retained, rather than assumed unreachable from spelling.
Named entities emit NAME, a DESCRIPTION; unnamed entities emit a DESCRIPTION.
The native article here is always a. Optional species adjective is creature RAW
field +0x60 through entity.race +0x98. The entity name is generated-name formatter
0xa946e0; type modifiers precede species. The full type switch is:
  0 civilization; 1 local government; 2 vessel; 3 migrating group;
  4 nomadic group; 5 religion; 6 military organization; 7 outcast group;
  8 performance troupe; 9 merchant company; 10 PROFESSION guild.
Absent guild member profession produces craft guild. Present profession comes
from 0x132cc10, not from English guessing or a fixed guild-name vocabulary.
The helper's chained unwind function is 0x132cc10..0x132e0b4. Its actual 135-way
0..134 built-in profession table is 0x132de98. It first uses 0x30cea0 to detect
creature/caste RAW PROFESSION_NAME overrides, and 0x30cf70 to select them;
0x30cf70 falls back from caste to the creature formatter 0x1bb330. These complete
native functions and switch operands are included in the new source graph.
Built-in profession 102 is STANDARD, with no noun: its table target 0x132de47
adds nothing for the singular guild call. Native art code still appends guild,
yielding bare guild unless a RAW profession name supplies text. A missing
profession (-1) instead takes the separate craft guild branch.

Shared item source boundary
---------------------------
The extraction retains the complete shared item description/name superset and
its cloth, dye, written-form/content/style, die-face, gemstone/material and
artifact identity suppliers. The finite 93-way item noun table, both 26-way
written-form tables and 18-way writing-style table are retained for both editions.
These supply image item elements or the physical source designation. The page
does not directly render every unrelated food, armor, book or dice detail on an
ordinary art-image element. Full item-title virtual bindings and later shared
item dependencies continue in the existing item-info-title/item-raw-title,
item-description-sources and symbol-picker-descriptions native source catalogs.
Dynamic RAW names, historical names, player nicknames, materials, quantity and
event data make complete paragraphs unbounded; all fixed native productions,
selectors, typed suppliers and their composition order are the extraction unit.
